payload.text: hv, 2026-10-27, directly to vc in vc's session, on the count rule, answering vc's question on 0113's 11,008 hits: "This is _BONKERS_. All I said was don't write guards or tests that compare against arbitrary magic numbers. HOW THE HELL HAS THIS TURNED INTO SOMETHING BIGGER THAN BEN HUR?!" and "This should simply be a sweep to get rid of magic numbers in tests and a rule not to add any into the future. The end. What is going on?!" vc's reading: the sweep is 0117 (the dispatch suites) and 0119 cut to the tests and guards outside them that compare against a written count; 0113 (prose, comments, test names) is withdrawn; strings, comments, test input and test names are out. The rule for the future lives in hv's global AGENTS.md (Molt-matts); its wording, which vc's decision 66 read as a sweep of everything, went to molt-vc for hv's OK of a narrower one, and Utilz writes no copy. The over-reach was vc's: decision 66 scoped from the rule's text without asking hv what it was for, and vc did not stop it as it grew.
